method: Ran the 5 locked tool prompts against model10/toolcall.onnx and model10/dpo.onnx with the exact production config (single-schema injection, seed 7, temp 0.7, top-p 0.9, max 64, maxToolRounds 1, onnxruntime-web WASM).

toolcall.verdict: 4/5 correct tool selection (p1-p5), all rounds complete with reason=end

dpo.p2: entered max-tool-rounds with malformed call {from:USD,to:US} (invalid 3-letter code) and generated 0 concluding tokens
dpo.verdict: 4/5 rounds complete; p2 fails the round and yields an empty concluding turn

reason: toolcall completes all five locked prompts with correct names and (after the p2 wording fix) correct arguments, ending cleanly. DPO's p2 breaks the one-tool-round rule (malformed 'US' code, zero-token conclusion). Tool selection on toolcall is also more reliable because the production catalog injects only the single required schema.
note: This supersedes the earlier numpy-RNG stage sweep note; the production mulberry32/seed-7 result is authoritative. Not a claim that DPO is unusable globally — only that toolcall is the cleaner presentation stage for the locked prompt set.
